info.title: Dinghy API
info.description: The widget API (`/v1/widget/{key}`, with the visitor's bearer token) and the operator API (`/v1/operator`, with the session cookie, or a workspace API key on the routes whose security lists `apiKey`). MCP lives at `/v1/mcp`, with an API key. Every error answer is `{ error: { code, message } }`, and clients branch on `code`. Sign-in lives at `/v1/auth`, a BetterAuth pass-through that is not part of the versioned API.

visitorToken.description: The browser token from POST /v1/widget/{key}/visitors, or a host token: an HS256 JWT that the host site signs with the workspace's signing secret.

sessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
sessionCookie.description: The session cookie that POST /v1/auth/magic-link/verify sets when it uses a sign-in link (BetterAuth). The cookie is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` on https. A write must also send the server's own Origin.

apiKey.description: A workspace API key, `dk_...`, that an owner or admin creates in Settings. It works only in its own workspace, with a member's permissions: read, search, reply, close, reopen and assign conversations. It needs no Origin.

example.body: Do you have a yearly plan?
Yes, it is two months free.

get.summary: Stream the visitor's messages after a cursor
get.description:
Server-sent events: `message` (its id is the new cursor, its data a Message), `ready` when caught up, `resync` to load from the start, and `close` with a reason. Read this with fetch, because EventSource cannot send the bearer token.

A `close` event's data is `{ reason }`: `lifetime` (the stream reached its 15-minute cap), `expired` (the host token expired), `revoked` (access was taken away, such as a block, a suspension or a removal), `unauthorized` (the token or session is no longer valid), `stopping` (the server is shutting down) or `error`. Reconnect from the last cursor, except after `unauthorized`, which needs a new token or sign-in.

post.summary: Report the page the visitor is on, for operators
post.description: The widget sends this when it loads and when the page's address changes, and only for a visitor who already has a token because they used the chat. The server stores something only for a visitor who has a conversation, and never creates a visitor here. It keeps the origin and path, never the query or hash, the title, when it came, and a short device line made from the User-Agent, which it does not keep. Each report adds a row to the visitor's page journey, unless it repeats the newest one, and a visitor keeps the newest 100.

post.summary: Send what the host page set with Dinghy.setContext(), for operators
post.description: Unsigned values from the host page, such as a plan or a cart total, that operators read next to the visitor. They are not verified. The widget sends them only for a visitor who has a token because they used the chat, and again after the first message. The server keeps them only for a visitor who has a conversation, and never creates a visitor here. Each report replaces the last one: at most 20 keys of 1 to 40 characters, with a string of up to 200 characters, a number, true, false or null as each value.

get.summary: Stream the workspace's changes after a cursor
get.description:
Server-sent events: `change` (its id is the new cursor), `ready` when caught up, `resync` to load everything again, and `close` with a reason. With no cursor, the stream starts at the present, so load the lists after `ready`.

A `change` event's data is `{ kind, conversationId }`, with `conversationId` null for a workspace change. A `message.created` change also has `fromVisitor`, true when the visitor wrote it. The kinds are `message.created`, `conversation.closed`, `conversation.reopened`, `conversation.assigned`, `conversation.deleted`, `conversation.moderated`, `team.changed` and `billing.changed`. A client reloads what the kind names, and ignores a kind it does not know.

A `close` event's data is `{ reason }`: `lifetime` (the stream reached its 15-minute cap), `expired` (the host token expired), `revoked` (access was taken away, such as a block, a suspension or a removal), `unauthorized` (the token or session is no longer valid), `stopping` (the server is shutting down) or `error`. Reconnect from the last cursor, except after `unauthorized`, which needs a new token or sign-in.

post.summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) over Streamable HTTP, stateless, with JSON answers
post.description: One JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request. Methods: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`. The tools are `list_conversations`, `search_conversations`, `get_conversation`, `reply`, `close_conversation`, `reopen_conversation` and `assign_conversation`, in the API key's workspace. A notification gets 202 with no body. A tool that fails answers with `isError: true` and the error's stable code. `GET` answers 405, because there is no event stream.

get.summary: Support numbers for the last 7, 30 or 90 days
get.description: Computed from the stored conversations and messages, for any member. A period runs from the start of the day, `days - 1` days ago, in `tz`, to now. Every number is about the conversations that started in it: a conversation's first reply time runs from its start to its first reply from an operator or an API key, and `operators` counts conversations by who sent that reply. A welcome chat on Dinghy Cloud counts nowhere.
